content.shloka:
Jāmavaṁta Ke Bachana Suhāe
Suni Hanumanta Hṛdaya Ati Bhāe
Taba Lagi Mohi Parikhehu Tumha Bhāī
Sahi Dukha Kaṁda Mūla Phala Khāī
content.meaning: Hearing the pleasant words of Jambavan, Hanuman's heart was greatly delighted. He said: Wait for me, brothers, enduring hardship and eating roots, tubers, and fruits.
content.transliteration:
Jāmavaṁta Ke Bacana Suhāe
Suni Hanumanta Hṛdaya Ati Bhāe
Taba Lagi Mohi Parikhehu Tumha Bhāī
Sahi Dukha Kaṁda Mūla Phala Khāī

content.shloka:
Jaba Lagi Āvauṁ Sītahi Dekhi
Hoihi Kāju Mohi Haraṣa Biśeṣī
Yaha Kahi Nāi Sabahi Kahu Māthā
Caleu Haraṣi Hiyaṁ Dhari Raghunāthā
content.meaning: Until I return after seeing Sita, the task shall be done — I feel immense joy. Saying this, bowing to all, he departed joyfully with Lord Raghunath in his heart.
content.transliteration:
Jaba Lagi Āvauṁ Sītahi Dekhi
Hoihi Kāju Mohi Haraṣa Biśeṣī
Yaha Kahi Nāi Sabahi Kahu Māthā
Caleu Haraṣi Hiyaṁ Dhari Raghunāthā

content.shloka:
Sindhu Tīra Eka Bhūdhara Sundarā
Kautuka Kūdi Caḍheu Tā Ūparā
Bāra Bāra Raghubīra Saṁbhārī
Tarakeu Pavanataney Bala Bhārī
content.meaning: On the seashore stood a beautiful mountain. Playfully he leaped upon it. Remembering Lord Rama again and again, the mighty son of the Wind-god soared across.
content.transliteration:
Sindhu Tīra Eka Bhūdhara Sundarā
Kautuka Kūdi Caḍheu Tā Ūparā
Bāra Bāra Raghubīra Saṁbhārī
Tarakeu Pavanataney Bala Bhārī

content.shloka:
Jehi Giri Charana Dei Hanumantā
Caleu So Gā Pātāla Turanta
Jimi Amōgha Raghupati Kara Bānā
Ehi Bhāṁti Caleu Hanumānā
content.meaning: The mountain on which Hanuman placed his foot immediately sank to the netherworld. Like the unfailing arrow of Lord Rama, thus did Hanuman fly forth.
content.transliteration:
Jehi Giri Caraṇa Dei Hanumantā
Caleu So Gā Pātāla Turanta
Jimi Amōgha Raghupati Kara Bānā
Ehi Bhāṁti Caleu Hanumānā

content.shloka:
Jalaṇidhi Raghupati Dūta Bichārī
Taiṁ Mainaka Hohi Śrama Hārī
Hanumāna Tēhi Parasa Kara Gayaū
Tāhi Rāma Kāju Kinha Bhalā Bhayaū
content.meaning: The ocean, recognizing Hanuman as Rama's messenger, asked Mount Mainaka to relieve his fatigue. Hanuman touched it and flew on — the mission of Rama was blessed.
content.transliteration:
Jalaṇidhi Raghupati Dūta Bicārī
Taiṁ Mainaka Hohi Śrama Hārī
Hanumāna Tēhi Parasa Kara Gayaū
Tāhi Rāma Kāju Kinha Bhalā Bhayaū

content.shloka:
Surasā Nāma Ahini Kai Mātā
Paṭhai Āsu Suranha Kari Bātā
Āi Kahī Mohi Bidhāta Bhojana Dinhā
content.meaning: Surasa, the mother of the serpents, was sent by the gods to test him. She approached and said: The Creator has granted you to me as food.
content.transliteration:
Surasā Nāma Ahini Kai Mātā
Paṭhai Āsu Suranha Kari Bātā
Āi Kahī Mohi Bidhātā Bhojana Dinhā

content.shloka:
Surasā Badana Paithī Puni Āvā
Sūkṣma Rūpa Dhari Āśisha Pāvā
Mohi Surahanha Jehi Kārana Paṭhāvā
Budhi Bala Maramu Tora Mai Pāvā
content.meaning: Entering and emerging from Surasa's mouth in a subtle form, he received her blessings. She said: The gods sent me to test you — I have witnessed your wisdom and strength.
content.transliteration:
Surasā Badana Paithī Puni Āvā
Sūkṣma Rūpa Dhari Āśiṣa Pāvā
Mohi Surahanha Jehi Kārana Paṭhāvā
Budhi Bala Maramu Tora Mai Pāvā

content.shloka:
Niśichari Ēka Siṁdhū Mahu Rahī
Kari Māyā Nabhū Ke Khaga Gahī
Jehi Kai Chāhāṁ Khaganā Grahī
Sō Siṁhikā Nāma Tāhi Hanumāna Māri Bidāī
content.meaning: A demoness lived in the ocean who would catch flying creatures by seizing their shadows. She was Simhika — Hanuman slew her and moved on.
content.transliteration:
Niśicari Ēka Siṁdhū Mahu Rahī
Kari Māyā Nabhū Ke Khaga Gahī
Jehi Kai Chāhāṁ Khaganā Grahī
Sō Siṁhikā Nāma Tāhi Hanumāna Māri Bidāī

content.shloka:
Tāhi Māri Marutasuta Bīrā
Jāi Pahũchā Laṁkāhiṁ Kapīrā
Laghu Rūpa Dhari Niśihi Gayaū
Laṁkā Kahu Kapihi Rakhavāraū
content.meaning: After slaying Simhika, the heroic son of the Wind-god reached Lanka. Assuming a tiny form at night, the monkey went forth. Lanka's guardian challenged him.
content.transliteration:
Tāhi Māri Marutasuta Bīrā
Jāi Pahũcā Laṁkāhiṁ Kapīrā
Laghu Rūpa Dhari Niśihi Gayaū
Laṁkā Kahu Kapihi Rakhavāraū

content.shloka:
Laṁkinī Hanu Mārai Kapi Tāhī
Bahuta Kṛpā Mōhi Prabhū Kī Āhī
Rāma Dūta Jānā Mai Terā
Jahi Jahi Laṁkā Saba Sujha Tera
content.meaning: Hanuman struck Lankini (the guardian goddess of Lanka), who then said: Great is the Lord's grace on me. I recognize you as Rama's messenger. Go freely through Lanka — all is open to you.
content.transliteration:
Laṁkinī Hanu Mārai Kapi Tāhī
Bahuta Kṛpā Mōhi Prabhū Kī Āhī
Rāma Dūta Jānā Mai Terā
Jahi Jahi Laṁkā Saba Sujhā Terā

content.shloka:
Masaka Samāna Rūpa Kapi Dharī
Laṁkahi Caleu Sumiria Naraharī
Nāma Leṭa Raghunātha Kā Chalā Hanumānā
Bhaya Nāśa Ṭanka Vihanṁga Samānā
content.meaning: Assuming a form as tiny as a mosquito, the monkey proceeded through Lanka, remembering Lord Narahari. Taking Raghunath's name, Hanuman moved fearlessly like a bird.
content.transliteration:
Masaka Samāna Rūpa Kapi Dharī
Laṁkahi Caleu Sumiri Naraharī
Nāma Leṭa Raghunātha Kā Calā Hanumānā
Bhaya Nāśa Ṭaṅka Vihaṅga Samānā

content.shloka:
Rāvaṇa Mandira Mahāṁ Dekhā
Bahu Mandira Sundarā Ati Rekhā
Sayana Kiyē Dekhe Bahu Nārī
Kahi Na Jāi Dasānana Śōbhā Bhārī
content.meaning: He saw Ravana's grand palace with many beautiful chambers. He saw many women asleep. The great splendor of the ten-headed one was beyond description.
content.transliteration:
Rāvaṇa Mandira Mahāṁ Dekhā
Bahu Mandira Sundarā Ati Rekhā
Sayana Kiyē Dekhe Bahu Nārī
Kahi Na Jāi Dasānana Śōbhā Bhārī

items.title: Doha 16-20: Finding Sita in Ashoka Vatika

content.shloka:
Kari Sōcha Hanumaṁta Mana Māhīṁ
Mahā Moṁha Mēṁ Sītā Nāhīṁ
Taba Hanumanta Bicharā Ura Māhīṁ
Gyāna Prakāśa Pragaṭā Tahāṁ
content.meaning: Hanuman thought in his mind: In this great delusion, Sita is not here. Then he reflected deeply and wisdom dawned within him.
content.transliteration:
Kari Sōca Hanumaṁta Mana Māhīṁ
Mahā Mōha Mēṁ Sītā Nāhīṁ
Taba Hanumanta Bicārā Ura Māhīṁ
Gyāna Prakāśa Pragaṭā Tahāṁ

content.shloka:
Aśōka Bāṭikā Māhīṁ Gayaū
Tahāṁ Dēkhī Sītā Dina Bhayaū
Kṛśa Tanu Sīya Rāma Guna Gāvati
Hṛdaya Sārikhē Prabhū Jānavati
content.meaning: He went to the Ashoka garden. There he saw Sita, sorrowful and thin. She was singing the virtues of Rama, knowing the Lord to be forever in her heart.
content.transliteration:
Aśōka Bāṭikā Māhīṁ Gayaū
Tahāṁ Dēkhī Sītā Dina Bhayaū
Kṛśa Tanu Sīya Rāma Guṇa Gāvati
Hṛdaya Sārikhē Prabhū Jānavati

content.shloka:
Trijatā Nāma Rākṣasī Ēkā
Rāma Charana Rati Nipuṇa Bibēkā
Sabahi Bōli Sumpyau Tabahī Sītā
Kahi Kahi Kathā Sunāi Punītā
content.meaning: A demoness named Trijata, devoted to Rama's feet and wise, was there. She pacified all the others and protected Sita, narrating the sacred stories again and again.
content.transliteration:
Trijaṭā Nāma Rākṣasī Ēkā
Rāma Caraṇa Rati Nipuṇa Bibēkā
Sabahi Bōli Sumpyau Tabahī Sītā
Kahi Kahi Kathā Sunāi Punītā

content.shloka:
Dēkhā Hanumaṁta Aśōka Tare
Sītā Baiṭhī Hari Dhyāna Lagāe
Kapi Hṛdaya Māhīṁ Ati Sukha Pāyau
Rāma Kāja Kīnhē Kapi Āyau
content.meaning: Hanuman saw under the Ashoka tree, Sita seated in meditation upon Hari. The monkey felt immense joy in his heart — for Rama's purpose, the monkey had arrived.
content.transliteration:
Dēkhā Hanumaṁta Aśōka Tare
Sītā Baiṭhī Hari Dhyāna Lagāe
Kapi Hṛdaya Māhīṁ Ati Sukha Pāyau
Rāma Kāja Kīnhē Kapi Āyau

content.shloka:
Rāma Nāma Mudrikā Rākhī
Giri Tē Ḍāri Sītā Ke Āgē
Nāma Dēkhi Sītā Harshāī
Mānō Aṁdhiyārē Mēṁ Dīpa Pāī
content.meaning: He dropped the ring bearing Rama's name from the tree before Sita. Seeing the name, Sita rejoiced as if finding a lamp in darkness.
content.transliteration:
Rāma Nāma Mudrikā Rākhī
Giri Tē Ḍāri Sītā Ke Āgē
Nāma Dēkhi Sītā Harṣāī
Mānō Aṁdhiyārē Mēṁ Dīpa Pāī

content.shloka:
Kapi Taha Āi Kahi Prāṇam Pranāmā
Mai Rāma Dūta Mama Nāma Hanumānā
Suni Sītā Harashi Ura Māhīṁ
Puni Puni Pūchati Kuśala Sab Bāhī
content.meaning: The monkey came there and with folded hands said: I am Rama's messenger, my name is Hanuman. Hearing this, Sita rejoiced in her heart and asked again and again about everyone's welfare.
content.transliteration:
Kapi Tahā Āi Kahi Prāṇam Pranāmā
Mai Rāma Dūta Mama Nāma Hanumānā
Suni Sītā Haraṣi Ura Māhīṁ
Puni Puni Pūchati Kuśala Saba Bāhī

content.shloka:
Kapihi Prāna Samā Prabhū Jānā
Sakala Kathā Kapihi Sunāyā
Kahahu Tāta Asa Mora Pranāmā
Sabahi Bhāṁti Prabhū Kṛpā Nidhanā
content.meaning: She knew Hanuman's devotion to the Lord was like his very life. The monkey narrated the entire story. She said: Tell the Lord my greetings — the treasure of mercy in every way.
content.transliteration:
Kapihi Prāṇa Samā Prabhū Jānā
Sakala Kathā Kapihi Sunāyā
Kahahu Tāta Asa Mora Pranāmā
Sabahi Bhāṁti Prabhū Kṛpā Nidhānā

content.shloka:
Mātu Mohi Dīje Kacchu Chīnhā
Jaise Raghunāthahi Dei Suhāvā
Sītā Dīnhī Cūḍāmaṇi Uttārī
Harashi Pavana Suta Kīnhī Durāī
content.meaning: The mother said: Give me some token of recognition. He said: Like something that will please Lord Raghunath. Sita removed her Chudamani (crest jewel) — Hanuman received it joyfully and kept it safe.
content.transliteration:
Mātu Mohi Dīje Kacchu Cīnhā
Jaise Raghunāthahi Dei Suhāvā
Sītā Dīnhī Cūḍāmaṇi Uttārī
Haraṣi Pavana Suta Kīnhī Durāī

content.shloka:
Kapi Bhayana Kaha Sunahu Bhavānī
Aśōka Bāṭikā Ujāṛī Gyānī
Pāna Taru Tōṛi Kapi Khāyā
Rachavāre Bahu Māre Āyā
content.meaning: Listen, O Bhavani — the wise monkey destroyed the Ashoka garden. He broke and ate the fruits of the trees, and when many guards came, he defeated them all.
content.transliteration:
Kapi Bhavana Kaha Sunahu Bhavānī
Aśōka Bāṭikā Ujāṛī Gyānī
Pāna Taru Tōṛi Kapi Khāyā
Rachavāre Bahu Māre Āyā

content.shloka:
Hanumaṁta Tabahī Gaḍha Tōrā
Bahu Rākṣasa Samara Mēṁ Jhōṛā
Bhūmi Parē Bahutaka Rākṣasa Bhārī
Kapi Bala Tejahu Atulita Bhārī
content.meaning: Hanuman then destroyed the fortress and crushed many Rakshasas in battle. Many mighty Rakshasas fell to the ground — the monkey's strength and valor were incomparable.
content.transliteration:
Hanumaṁta Tabahī Gaḍha Tōrā
Bahu Rākṣasa Samara Mēṁ Jhōṛā
Bhūmi Parē Bahutaka Rākṣasa Bhārī
Kapi Bala Tejahu Atulita Bhārī

content.shloka:
Akṣay Kumāra Māri Saṁhārā
Rāvaṇa Krodhit Bahu Bicārā
Meghnad Paṭhāyā Rana Māhī
Brahmastra Bāṁdhā Kapi Tāhī
content.meaning: He slew Akshay Kumar in destruction. Ravana, enraged, deliberated much. He sent Meghanada (Indrajit) to the battle, who bound the monkey with the Brahmastra.
content.transliteration:
Akṣay Kumāra Māri Saṁhārā
Rāvaṇa Krodhita Bahu Bicārā
Meghnad Paṭhāyā Raṇa Māhī
Brahmāstra Bāṁdhā Kapi Tāhī

content.shloka:
Brahmā Ke Bachan Samujhi Kapirāī
Baṁdhana Kāṭi Na Sakai Koī Bhāī
Jāni Budhhi Bala Nipuṇa Hanumānā
Rāvaṇa Sabhā Gayeu Bhagavānā
content.meaning: Understanding Brahma's word, the monkey king knew none could break that bond. Knowing his own wisdom and might, the divine Hanuman went to Ravana's court.
content.transliteration:
Brahmā Ke Bacan Samujhi Kapirāī
Baṁdhana Kāṭi Na Sakai Koī Bhāī
Jāni Budhi Bala Nipuṇa Hanumānā
Rāvaṇa Sabhā Gayeu Bhagavānā

content.shloka:
Kapi Bandha Āyau Rāvana Pāhī
Krodha Kaha Kahu Kīsa Kahāṁ Se Āhī
Mai Raghubīra Dūta Mai Bānī
Āyau Suni Sītā Kī Kahānī
content.meaning: The bound monkey was brought before Ravana. In anger Ravana asked: Monkey, where have you come from? I am the messenger of Lord Rama — I came hearing the story of Sita.
content.transliteration:
Kapi Bandha Āyau Rāvaṇa Pāhī
Krodha Kaha Kahu Kīsa Kahāṁ Se Āhī
Mai Raghubīra Dūta Mai Bānī
Āyau Suni Sītā Kī Kahānī

content.shloka:
Sunu Rāvaṇa Brahmāṇḍa Nikāyā
Pāu Mahā Eka Prabhūhi Upāyā
Jākē Bala Biraṁci Hari Īsā
Pālata Srujata Harata Daśasīśā
content.meaning: Listen Ravana, the many universes — each born of a single device of my Lord. By whose power Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva create, sustain, and destroy, O ten-headed one.
content.transliteration:
Sunu Rāvaṇa Brahmāṇḍa Nikāyā
Pāu Mahā Eka Prabhūhi Upāyā
Jāke Bala Biraṁci Hari Īsā
Pālata Srujata Harata Daśasīśā

content.shloka:
Kahi Kahi Kathā Gyāna Upadēśā
Rāvaṇa Jvalita Bhayau Ati Krōśā
Kapi Kī Pūṁchahi Lāgahu Āgī
Satya Kahī Puni Jārahu Āgī
content.meaning: Despite Hanuman's stories and wisdom teachings, Ravana burned with rage. He ordered: Set fire to the monkey's tail! The truth was spoken, yet they set fire to it.
content.transliteration:
Kahi Kahi Kathā Gyāna Upadēśā
Rāvaṇa Jvalita Bhayau Ati Krōśā
Kapi Kī Pūṁcahi Lāgahu Āgī
Satya Kahī Puni Jārahu Āgī

content.shloka:
Pavana Tanay Bala Pavan Samānā
Jārā Laṁkā Saba Bahu Bidhānā
Kūdā Sindhu Mahin Bujhāī Pūṁchā
Bhaye Prakṛta Puni Kapi Kīnhā Sūchā
content.meaning: The son of the Wind, powerful as the wind itself, burned all of Lanka in many ways. He leaped into the ocean to extinguish his tail, returned to his natural form, and felt satisfaction.
content.transliteration:
Pavana Tanay Bala Pavana Samānā
Jārā Laṁkā Saba Bahu Bidhānā
Kūdā Sindhu Mahiṁ Bujhāī Pūṁcā
Bhaye Prakṛta Puni Kapi Kīnhā Sūcā

content.shloka:
Puni Sītahi Dekhi Ḍara Māhīṁ
Jānakī Kahu Agni Nahi Lāhīṁ
Puni Kahi Trijatā Saba Sunāī
Īśvara Kṛpā Mahi Sītā Sahāī
content.meaning: Then seeing Sita, fear arose — has the fire harmed Janaki? But Trijata announced to all that by God's grace, Sita was unharmed and protected.
content.transliteration:
Puni Sītahi Dekhi Ḍara Māhīṁ
Jānakī Kahu Agni Nahi Lāhīṁ
Puni Kahi Trijaṭā Saba Sunāī
Īśvara Kṛpā Mahi Sītā Sahāī

content.shloka:
Kapi Āyau Sītā Ke Pāhī
Sīya Saṁdēśa Dīnhā Saba Kāhī
Kahu Kapihi Rākhahu Hṛdaya Bisālā
Kari Praṇāma Caleu Tattakālā
content.meaning: The monkey came before Sita. Sita gave her message for all. She told the monkey: Keep this in your great heart. Bowing in reverence, he departed at once.
content.transliteration:
Kapi Āyau Sītā Ke Pāhī
Sīya Saṁdēśa Dīnhā Saba Kāhī
Kahu Kapihi Rākhahu Hṛdaya Bisālā
Kari Praṇāma Caleu Tattakālā

content.shloka:
Calā Hanumāna Ā Laghukāī
Parvata Upar Baiṭhā Āī
Hari Hṛdaya Rākhī Sab Bātā
Jay Raghunātha Dīna Ke Tātā
content.meaning: Hanuman flew with swift speed and alighted upon the mountain. He kept all matters in his heart dedicated to Hari. Victory to Raghunatha, the protector of the humble!
content.transliteration:
Calā Hanumāna Ā Laghukāī
Parvata Upara Baiṭhā Āī
Hari Hṛdaya Rākhī Saba Bātā
Jaya Raghunātha Dīna Ke Tātā

content.shloka:
Sunahu Bhavānī Prabhū Kai Kṛpā
Jaki Balā Agni Bujhāī
Sītā Rakṣā Kari Kēsarī Nandanā
Kāryā Siddhi Karī Bhagavānā
content.meaning: Listen Bhavani, by the Lord's grace whose power extinguished the fire — Sita was protected by the son of Kesari. The divine one accomplished the mission.
content.transliteration:
Sunahu Bhavānī Prabhū Kai Kṛpā
Jaki Balā Agni Bujhāī
Sītā Rakṣā Kari Kēsarī Nandanā
Kāryā Siddhi Karī Bhagavānā

content.shloka:
Harashi Parā Sāgara Uttarā
Āi Pahũchā Giri Pāra Utārā
Kapinha Kapihi Milā Sab Dhāī
Haraṣa Bhayau Saba Kapihi Sunāī
content.meaning: Joyfully he crossed the ocean and arrived back at the mountain shore. All the monkeys rushed to meet him — there was great joy as the monkey narrated everything.
content.transliteration:
Haraṣi Parā Sāgara Uttarā
Āi Pahũcā Giri Pāra Utārā
Kapinha Kapihi Milā Saba Dhāī
Haraṣa Bhayau Saba Kapihi Sunāī

content.shloka:
Suni Sītā Duḥkha Prabhū Sukha Pāyā
Bahu Praśansā Kapi Kō Sunāyā
Kapi Ke Dekhā Hari Ānandā
Milā Prabhū Kapihi Uraṁ Lagāyā
content.meaning: Hearing of Sita's sorrow, the Lord felt compassion. He praised the monkey greatly. Seeing the monkey, Hari felt bliss and embraced him to His chest.
content.transliteration:
Suni Sītā Duḥkha Prabhū Sukha Pāyā
Bahu Praśansā Kapi Kō Sunāyā
Kapi Ke Dekhā Hari Ānandā
Milā Prabhū Kapihi Uraṁ Lagāyā

content.shloka:
Kahahu Tāta Kapihi Saba Kathā
Sītā Kahu Kahu Kaisi Byathā
Kapi Kahā Sunu Rāma Kṛpālā
Dekhi Mudrikā Harashi Bisālā
content.meaning: Tell me everything, O friend — describe Sita's anguish. The monkey said: Listen, compassionate Rama. Seeing the ring, she rejoiced greatly.
content.transliteration:
Kahahu Tāta Kapihi Saba Kathā
Sītā Kahu Kahu Kaisi Byathā
Kapi Kahā Sunu Rāma Kṛpālā
Dekhi Mudrikā Haraṣi Bisālā

content.shloka:
Suni Kapi Bachan Rāma Man Bhāyau
Śrī Prabhū Kapihi Uraṁ Lāyau
Bāra Bāra Kapi Karahin Pranāmā
Prabhu Ke Rūpa Ākhē Abhirāmā
content.meaning: Hearing the monkey's words, Rama's heart was pleased. The Lord embraced the monkey to His chest. Again and again the monkey bowed — the Lord's form was supremely beautiful.
content.transliteration:
Suni Kapi Bacana Rāma Mana Bhāyau
Śrī Prabhū Kapihi Uraṁ Lāyau
Bāra Bāra Kapi Karahiṁ Pranāmā
Prabhu Ke Rūpa Ākhē Abhirāmā

content.shloka:
Śrī Gaṇeśāya Namaḥ
Śrī Hanumān Jī Kō Praṇāma Kari
Sundarakāṇḍa Pāṭha Ārambha Karēṁ
content.meaning: Salutations to Lord Ganesha. After bowing to Lord Hanuman, begin the recitation of Sundarkand.
content.transliteration:
Śrī Gaṇeśāya Namaḥ
Śrī Hanumān Jī Kō Praṇāma Kari
Sundarakāṇḍa Pāṭha Ārambha Karēṁ

content.shloka:
Sankalpa: Śrī Rāma Prītyartham Sundara Kāṇḍa Pāṭham Aham Kariṣye
Dīpam Jvālayitvā Lāla Vastra Āsana Sthāpayēt
content.meaning: Resolve: For the pleasure of Lord Rama, I shall recite Sundarkand. Light a lamp and place a red cloth seat for the recitation.
content.transliteration:
Saṅkalpa: Śrī Rāma Prītyartham Sundara Kāṇḍa Pāṭham Aham Kariṣye
Dīpam Jvālayitvā Lāla Vastra Āsana Sthāpayet

content.shloka:
Pāṭha Samāpti Ke Bād:
Śrī Hanumān Chālīsā Paṭhēṁ
Āratī Karēṁ Aur Prasāda Vitaraṇa Karēṁ
content.meaning: After completing the recitation: Recite Sri Hanuman Chalisa. Perform Aarti and distribute Prasad.
content.transliteration:
Pāṭha Samāpti Ke Bād:
Śrī Hanumān Cālīsā Paṭhēṁ
Āratī Karēṁ Aur Prasāda Vitaraṇa Karēṁ

content.shloka:
Maṅgala Bhavana Amangala Hārī
Dravahu So Dasaratha Ajira Bihārī
Pavana Tanaya Santan Hitakārī
Hṛdaya Birājahu Rāma Sārī
content.meaning: O auspicious one who removes all inauspiciousness, O beloved who plays in Dasharatha's courtyard, have mercy! O son of the Wind, benefactor of the saints, may Rama with Sita reside in our hearts forever.
content.transliteration:
Maṅgala Bhavana Amaṅgala Hārī
Dravahu So Dasaratha Ajira Bihārī
Pavana Tanaya Santan Hitakārī
Hṛdaya Birājahu Rāma Sārī
